content: I never felt a 'click' when any of the tool heads were pushed onto the hotend. But continued past this step regardless
I had to remove some plastic material from 2 of the docks to make the calibration work. There was some plastic sticking out that had to be cut away.
hmmm during shaper calibration i noticed the 4th tool was tilted in it's spot.. off its orientation.... has me slightly worried
Take a good look, sometimes the tools is slightly crocked, tilted to the side. so shove the toolhead onto it straight, and tighten the screw!

replies.content: we need better instructions what to do if X is misaligned in either direction or Y. Very confusing at the moment.

content: So if you get a dock calibration failure (difference is higher than 1 mm), I fixed this by loosening the silver screws (against what was said) so that it is closer to the toolholder (mine was too far away). So either tighten or loosen the screws depending on what the difference is.

replies.content: Same here. I also assumed the screws needed to be tightened, based on instructions.  I was also off by 1+ mm on x and y.   I also needed to be somewhat loose, by 1 to 2 full turns loose from snug.  There needs to be some obvious very slight wiggle. In fact, after doing this, and successfully completing the calibration on all nozzles, it said to loosen them all by one full turn.  This also implied it needs some wiggle room to move around.  The instructions stating to tighten when done is ambiguous and confusing.  Is it tighten or loosen?  Freak if I know.  I just know what works for me.  Loose it is for me, with the wiggles….. until Prusa makes an update I guess.

At the end of doc calibration it does say to loosen all of the screws by 1 full turn.. Seems odd to keep them loose for install, tighten for cal, then loosen again after cal. But whatever works I guess, no issues for me in the calibration on any steps :)
